paragraphs: We are a biopharmaceutical company developing potential first- or best-in-class, high-impact therapies for autoimmune diseases and cancer. We pursue promising therapeutic targets while leveraging core expertise in T cell engagers, which are established in oncology and are now advancing into autoimmune diseases. With a clinical-stage pipeline built on a rigorous scientific approach and purposeful innovation, we are advancing our mission to deliver new standards of care for patients. Our current programs are summarized in the diagram and bullets below:

• CLN-978 is a CD19xCD3 bispecific T cell engager that we are developing for autoimmune diseases. In the Phase 1 OUTRACE Program, CLN-978 is being evaluated in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus ("SLE"), rheumatoid arthritis ("RA"), and Sjögren's disease ("SjD"). The OUTRACE SLE Study is an ongoing global Phase 1 clinical trial in patients with moderate to severe SLE. The OUTRACE RA Study is a Phase 1 clinical trial in patients with active, difficult-to-treat RA, which is ongoing in Europe. We plan to share initial clinical data in SLE and RA in the second quarter of 2026 and repeat dosing data in RA in the third quarter of 2026. The OUTRACE SjD Study is an ongoing global Phase 1 clinical trial in patients with active, moderate to severe Sjögren's disease. We plan to share initial clinical data in Sjögren's disease in the fourth quarter of 2026.

• Velinotamig is a BCMAxCD3 bispecific T cell engager that we are developing for autoimmune diseases. Chongqing Genrix Biopharmaceutical Co., Ltd. ("Genrix"), from which we licensed velinotamig, is enrolling a Phase 1 clinical trial in China in patients with autoimmune diseases, initially in patients with SLE, followed by planned future expansion into other indications, and initial clinical data will be shared in the fourth quarter of 2026. We intend to use the data generated from this Phase 1 clinical trial to accelerate global clinical development. Following the completion of the Genrix Phase 1 clinical trial, we will conduct all further development of velinotamig in autoimmune diseases.

• CLN-049 is a FLT3xCD3 bispecific T cell engager. CLN-049 is being evaluated in an ongoing Phase 1 clinical trial in patients with relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia ("AML") or myelodysplastic syndrome ("MDS"). At the 2025 American Society for Hematology ("ASH") Annual Meeting, we shared monotherapy efficacy data from the ongoing dose escalation portion of the trial in a heavily pretreated all-comer population of patients with relapsed/refractory AML. We plan to share a clinical data update from the dose escalation portion of the trial in the second half of 2026. We also plan to begin enrolling dose expansion cohorts in the second quarter of 2026 and expect to complete enrollment in the fourth quarter of 2026 to determine the recommended Phase 2 dose for an expected single-arm pivotal registrational trial.

• Zipalertinib (CLN-081/TAS6417), on which we are collaborating with an affiliate of Taiho Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. ("Taiho"), is an orally-available small-molecule, irreversible epidermal growth factor receptor ("EGFR") inhibitor that is designed to selectively target cells expressing EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations ("EGFR ex20ins") with relative sparing of cells expressing wild-type EGFR.

o We are evaluating zipalertinib in the pivotal Phase 2b portion of the REZILIENT1 clinical trial in patients with EGFR ex20ins non-small cell lung cancer ("NSCLC") who progressed after prior systemic therapy. In February 2026, based on the primary efficacy data from REZILIENT1, Taiho completed a rolling submission of a new drug application ("NDA") seeking accelerated approval of zipalertinib for the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR ex20ins NSCLC who have previously received platinum-based systemic chemotherapy.

o Taiho is evaluating zipalertinib in a global Phase 3 clinical trial ("REZILIENT3") in combination with chemotherapy as a potential first-line treatment for locally advanced or metastatic EGFR ex20ins NSCLC adult patients. Taiho completed enrollment of the trial in February 2026 and expects to obtain top-line results by the end of 2026.

o Taiho is also evaluating zipalertinib in a Phase 2 parallel cohort trial ("REZILIENT2"). Taiho shared emerging data from certain REZILIENT2 cohorts at the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer ("IASLC") 2025 World Conference on Lung Cancer ("WCLC") and European Society for Medical Oncology ("ESMO") Congress 2025.
Our strategy is to accelerate potential first- or best-in-class, high-impact therapies in autoimmune diseases and cancer. The key objectives we aim to achieve with our strategy are as follows:

• Explore the broad potential of CLN-978 in autoimmune diseases. Academic investigators and industry sponsors have published data across a variety of molecular targets and modalities highlighting the potential for a CD19xCD3 T cell engager to achieve sustained improvements in disease manifestations, including durable remission from symptoms in some cases, in multiple autoimmune disease indications, including SLE and RA. We believe that CLN-978 is highly-differentiated and has several potential advantages relative to other CD19-directed therapies currently in development, including monoclonal antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor T cell ("CAR T") therapies, as well as other T cell engagers, such as off-the-shelf subcutaneous administration and the ability to redirect T cells to lyse B cells expressing very low levels of CD19. We are therefore exploring the broad development of CLN-978 in autoimmune diseases.

• Advance CLN-049 for the treatment of a broad population of AML patients. The AML treatment paradigm is currently fragmented, and there are limited treatment options that are broadly applicable across AML subpopulations. Recent approvals are for small-molecule targeted therapies that address only smaller genetic and molecular subsets of AML. CLN-049 binds both mutated and wild-type FLT3, which is expressed on AML blasts in more than 80% of AML patients. Consequently, CLN-049 has the potential to address a broad population of AML patients without need for biomarker testing. We plan to advance CLN-049 into dose expansion in relapsed AML patients to determine a recommended Phase 2 dose for an expected single-arm pivotal registrational trial. We will also explore CLN-049 as a potential frontline treatment in combination with current standard-of-care treatment for patients with newly diagnosed AML.

• Unlock the near-term non-dilutive financial benefits of zipalertinib. In collaboration with Taiho, we are pursuing a broad, parallel development plan designed to exploit the potential of zipalertinib in multiple patient populations in the REZILIENT program. As zipalertinib is advanced closer to regulatory approvals and commercialization by Taiho, we move closer to potentially achieving certain non-dilutive financial benefits. Under an agreement with Taiho, we are eligible to receive $30.0 million and up to $100.0 million in payments from Taiho tied to United States ("U.S.") regulatory approvals in second-line and first-line EGFR ex20ins NSCLC, respectively. We are also eligible to receive 50% of any future pre-tax profits from potential U.S. sales of zipalertinib. We plan to use the potential proceeds from zipalertinib through our collaboration with Taiho to continue to advance the development of our priority programs, CLN-978 and CLN-049.

CLN-978 is a half-life extended, humanized, single-chain bispecific T cell engager designed to simultaneously engage CD19 on B cells and CD3 on T cells, triggering redirected T cells to lyse B cells. CLN-978 contains two tandemly arranged single-chain variable fragments ("scFvs") for CD19 and CD3 and a third domain in the form of a single-domain antibody (VHH) for binding to human serum albumin ("HSA") to prolong its serum half-life. CLN-978 demonstrated potency in both redirecting T cells to lyse low-CD19 expressing cells in vitro and activity in mice in B cell lymphoma models in vivo. In preclinical in vivo studies in non-human primates, treatment with CLN-978 at low doses led to profound B cell depletion in peripheral blood even after a single dose, and deep B cell depletion in lymphoid tissues was observed with multi-dose treatment. CLN-978 displayed similar induction of target B cell killing, T cell activation, and cytokine production in peripheral blood mononuclear cells derived from patients with SLE, RA or Sjögren's as compared to healthy volunteers. We believe together these preclinical results support evaluation of CLN-978 for the treatment of B cell-mediated autoimmune diseases.

B cells express the CD19 target and play a role in numerous autoimmune diseases which can affect multiple organ systems. Common to the pathophysiology of these disorders is the aberrant production of antibodies directed toward self-antigens, which are referred to as autoantibodies. Academic investigators and industry sponsors have published data across a variety of molecular targets and modalities demonstrating the potential for a CD19xCD3 T cell engager to achieve sustained improvements in disease manifestations, including durable remission from symptoms in some cases, in multiple treatment resistant autoimmune disease indications, including SLE and RA. These clinical data show that the profound depletion of B cells by CD19-directed therapy, followed by the re-emergence of a naïve B cell repertoire, effects a "reset" of the B cell compartment and a lasting elimination of autoreactive antibodies.

headings: Risks Related to the Development of Our Product Candidates
We may encounter substantial delays in preclinical studies and clinical trials or may not be able to conduct or complete preclinical studies or clinical trials on the expected timelines, if at all.
Difficulty in enrolling patients has delayed, and in the future could delay or prevent, clinical trials of our product candidates and ultimately delay or prevent regulatory approval.

We are currently conducting and may in the future conduct clinical trials for product candidates outside the U.S., and the FDA and comparable foreign regulatory authorities may not accept data from such trials.
We may develop product candidates in combination with other therapies, which would expose us to additional risks.
Risks Related to Our Financial Condition and Capital Requirements
Our limited operating history may make it difficult for you to evaluate the success of our business to date and to assess our future viability.
We have incurred significant losses since inception, and we expect to incur losses over the next several years and may not be able to achieve or sustain revenues or profitability in the future.
We have not generated any revenue from the sale of our product candidates and may never be profitable.

If we engage in acquisitions or strategic partnerships, this may increase our capital requirements, dilute our stockholders, cause us to incur debt or assume contingent liabilities, and subject us to other risks.
paragraphs: The following information should be read in conjunction with the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could harm our business, financial condition or future results, and such risk factors may not be the only risks we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial also may adversely affect our business, financial condition or future results. See "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Our preclinical studies and clinical trials may fail to demonstrate adequately the safety and efficacy of any of our product candidates, which would prevent or delay development, regulatory approval, and commercialization.

Before obtaining regulatory approvals for the commercial sale of our current and future product candidates, we must demonstrate the safety and efficacy of our investigational product candidates for use in each target indication through lengthy, complex, and expensive preclinical studies and clinical trials. If the results of our ongoing or future preclinical studies and clinical trials are inconclusive with respect to the safety and efficacy of our product candidates, if we do not meet the clinical endpoints with statistical and clinically meaningful significance, or if there are safety concerns associated with our product candidates, we may be prevented or delayed in obtaining marketing approval for such product candidates. In some instances, there can be significant variability in safety or efficacy results between different preclinical studies and clinical trials of the same product candidate due to numerous factors, including changes in and adherence to clinical trial procedures set forth in protocols, differences in the size and type of the patient populations, and the rate of dropout among clinical trial participants.

Additionally, we and third parties may have limited preclinical and clinical data, and a more limited understanding generally, with respect to certain indications for which our product candidates are being developed, including autoimmune diseases, and we cannot predict the extent to which the safety and efficacy of a product candidate may vary across indications. We may encounter significant challenges creating appropriate models and assays for evaluating the safety and efficacy of our product candidates and may not be able to provide sufficient data or other evidence, to the satisfaction of regulatory authorities, that certain unexpected results observed in preclinical and clinical testing of our product candidates are not indicative of the potential safety issues of such product candidates. We may develop program plans and timelines for certain product candidates based on our experience with such product candidates in different indications or with other product candidates that incorporate or were developed with the same technologies based on our expectation that such product candidates will perform and act similarly. However, our product candidates may reveal unexpected, important differences, including with respect to safety or efficacy, when developed in different indications or as compared to such other product candidates, including differences that may require changes to the manufacturing process or clinical development plan that require additional time and resources beyond what we initially anticipated. Any such occurrence could require us to adjust or alter our development plans, which could delay, harm, or prevent our ability to develop and commercialize or receive regulatory approval for such product candidates.

In addition to our ongoing clinical trials of zipalertinib, patients have been, and will likely continue to be, treated with zipalertinib under an expanded access or "compassionate use" program. To the extent the experiences of patients being treated in this program are inconsistent with or less favorable than the results of our ongoing or planned company-sponsored clinical trials with zipalertinib, it may negatively affect perceptions of zipalertinib, our other product candidates, or our business. In addition, the United States ("U.S.") Food and Drug Administration (the "FDA"), or foreign regulatory authorities may require us to obtain and submit additional clinical data due to these inconsistent or unfavorable results, which could delay clinical development or marketing approval of zipalertinib or potentially our other product candidates.

Preclinical and clinical development involves a lengthy and expensive process with an uncertain outcome, and results of earlier studies and trials may not be predictive of future preclinical studies or clinical trial results. If our preclinical studies and clinical trials are not sufficient to support regulatory approval of any of our product candidates, we may incur additional costs or experience delays in completing, or ultimately be unable to complete, the development of such product candidate.

CLN-617 is an interleukin-2 and interleukin-12 fusion protein that we were previously evaluating in a Phase 1 clinical trial. In November 2025, after a review of the emerging clinical data in patients with advanced solid tumors, we discontinued further development of CLN-617.

paragraphs: 本公司為一生物科技公司，致力於開發具潛力之首創或最佳治療選擇、高影響力療法，用以治療自身免疫疾病與癌症。本公司追求具潛力之治療目標，同時善用在T細胞活化劑之核心專業知識，該技術已於腫瘤學領域建立，並正進展至自身免疫疾病。本公司以嚴謹科學方法與有意圖之創新為基礎，建立臨牀階段之產品線，持續推動本公司使命，即為病患提供新的照護標準。本公司目前之計畫於下圖與項目說明中進行總結：

• CLN-978為一CD19xCD3雙特異性T細胞活化劑，本公司正開發用以治療自身免疫疾病。在Phase 1 OUTRACE計畫中，CLN-978正在評估於患有系統性紅斑狼瘡（"SLE"）、類風濕性關節炎（"RA"）及史格倫症（"SjD"）之病患。OUTRACE SLE研究為一持續進行之全球Phase 1臨牀試驗，針對中度至重度SLE病患。OUTRACE RA研究為一Phase 1臨牀試驗，針對活動性且難治性RA病患，目前於歐洲進行中。本公司預計於2026年第二季分享SLE與RA之初步臨牀數據，並於2026年第三季分享RA之重複給藥數據。OUTRACE SjD研究為一持續進行之全球Phase 1臨牀試驗，針對活動性且中度至重度史格倫症病患。本公司預計於2026年第四季分享史格倫症之初步臨牀數據。

• Velinotamig為一BCMAxCD3雙特異性T細胞活化劑，本公司正開發用以治療自身免疫疾病。重慶基因瑞生物製藥股份有限公司（"Genrix"），本公司自其取得velinotamig之授權，正在中國進行一Phase 1臨牀試驗，針對患有自身免疫疾病之病患，初期於SLE病患中進行，未來預計擴展至其他適應症，並於2026年第四季分享初步臨牀數據。本公司有意利用此Phase 1臨牀試驗所產生之數據，加速全球臨牀發展。完成Genrix Phase 1臨牀試驗後，本公司將進行velinotamig在自身免疫疾病之所有進一步發展。

• CLN-049為一FLT3xCD3雙特異性T細胞活化劑。CLN-049正在進行一持續進行之Phase 1臨牀試驗，針對患有復發/難治性急性髓細胞白血病（"AML"）或骨髓增生異常綜合症（"MDS"）之病患。於2025年美國血液學會（"ASH"）年會中，本公司分享了來自持續進行之劑量遞增部分之單藥療效數據，針對曾接受多線治療之所有來源病患羣，患有復發/難治性AML。本公司預計於2026年下半年分享來自劑量遞增部分之臨牀數據更新。本公司亦預計於2026年第二季開始納入劑量擴展羣組，並預計於2026年第四季完成納入，以確定推薦之Phase 2劑量，用於預期之單臂關鍵性註冊臨牀試驗。
• Zipalertinib（CLN-081/TAS6417），本公司與太和製藥股份有限公司（"Taiho"）之子公司合作開發，為一口服小分子、不可逆之表皮生長因子受體（"EGFR"）抑制劑，設計用以選擇性地針對表現EGFR exon 20插入突變（"EGFR ex20ins"）之細胞，同時相對保留表現野生型EGFR之細胞。

o 本公司正在評估zipalertinib於REZILIENT1臨牀試驗之關鍵Phase 2b部分，針對曾接受過系統性治療後進展之EGFR ex20ins非小細胞肺腺癌（"NSCLC"）病患。於2026年2月，根據REZILIENT1之主要療效數據，太和完成滾動提交新藥申請（"NDA"），以尋求zipalertinib用於治療曾接受含鉑系統化學治療之局部晚期或轉移性EGFR ex20ins NSCLC病患之加速核准。
o 太和正在評估zipalertinib於一全球Phase 3臨牀試驗（"REZILIENT3"）中，與化療藥物合併使用，作為局部晚期或轉移性EGFR ex20ins NSCLC成人病患之潛在一線治療。太和於2026年2月完成該試驗之納入，預計於2026年底取得初步結果。
o 太和亦正在評估zipalertinib於一Phase 2平行羣組試驗（"REZILIENT2"）。太和於國際肺癌研究協會（"IASLC"）2025世界肺癌會議（"WCLC"）及歐洲醫學腫瘤學會（"ESMO"）2025年大會中，分享了來自REZILIENT2部分羣組之初步數據。
本公司策略為加速潛在的第一線或最佳治療選擇、高影響力療法在自身免疫疾病與癌症的應用。我們透過此策略旨在達成的關鍵目標如下：

• 探索 CLN-978 在自身免疫疾病中的廣泛潛力。學術研究者與產業贊助方已發表資料，涵蓋多種分子目標與治療方式，顯示 CD19xCD3 T 細胞活化劑有潛力在多種自身免疫疾病指標中，包括紅斑狼瘡（SLE）與類風濕性關節炎（RA），實現持續改善疾病表現，包括在某些情況下達成長期症狀緩解。本公司認為 CLN-978 具有高度差異性，相較於目前在開發中的其他 CD19 導向療法，包括單株抗體、嵌合抗原受體 T 細胞（"CAR T"）療法，以及其他 T 細胞活化劑，如現成的皮下給藥方式，以及能將 T 細胞重新導向以裂解表達非常低水平 CD19 的 B 細胞。因此，本公司正在探索 CLN-978 在自身免疫疾病中的廣泛開發。

• 推進 CLN-049 用於治療廣泛的 AML 患者族羣。目前 AML 治療模式分散，且缺乏廣泛適用於 AML 子族羣的治療選擇。近期核准的治療為小分子標靶藥物，僅針對 AML 的較小基因與分子亞羣。CLN-049 可與突變及野生型 FLT3 結合，而 FLT3 在超過 80% 的 AML 患者中於 AML 原始細胞上表達。因此，CLN-049 有潛力在不需生物標記測試的情況下，治療廣泛的 AML 患者族羣。本公司計畫將 CLN-049 推進至復發 AML 患者中的劑量擴展階段，以確定推薦的第二期臨牀試驗劑量，並預期進行單臂關鍵性註冊試驗。本公司也會探討 CLN-049 作為潛在一線治療，在與現行標準治療組合使用下，用於新診斷 AML 患者。

• 解鎖 zipalertinib 的近期非稀釋財務效益。與 Taiho 合作，本公司正在進行廣泛且並行的開發計畫，以利用 zipalertinib 在 REZILIENT 計畫中多個患者族羣的潛力。隨著 zipalertinib 靠近 Taiho 的監管核准與商業化，本公司將更接近實現某些非稀釋財務效益。根據與 Taiho 的協議，本公司有資格獲得來自 Taiho 的 30.0 百萬美元，以及在美國（"U.S.") 監管核准於第二線與第一線 EGFR ex20ins NSCLC 分別達成 100.0 百萬美元的付款。本公司也有資格獲得任何未來美國銷售 zipalertinib 的預稅利潤的 50%。本公司計畫透過與 Taiho 的合作，利用 zipalertinib 的潛在資金，持續推進本公司優先計畫 CLN-978 與 CLN-049 的開發。

CLN-978 是一種半衰期延長、人類化、單鏈雙特異性 T 細胞活化劑，設計用以同時與 B 細胞上的 CD19 和 T 細胞上的 CD3 結合，引發重新導向的 T 細胞裂解 B 細胞。CLN-978 含有兩個串聯排列的單鏈變體片段（"scFvs"）用於 CD19 和 CD3，以及一個以單域抗體（VHH）形式存在的第三域，用於與人血清白蛋白（"HSA"）結合以延長其血漿半衰期。CLN-978 在體外引導 T 細胞裂解低 CD19 表達細胞以及在 B 細胞淋巴瘤模型中體內顯示活性。在非人靈長類動物的體內預臨牀研究中，以低劑量治療 CLN-978 可導致單次劑量後外周血液中 B 細胞顯著減少，且多劑量治療後淋巴組織中 B 細胞深度減少。CLN-978 在來自紅斑狼瘡（SLE）、類風濕性關節炎（RA）或史格倫症（Sjögren's）患者以及健康志願者的外周血液單核細胞中，顯示與健康志願者相似的目標 B 細胞殺傷、T 細胞活化及細胞因子產生。本公司認為這些預臨牀結果支持評估 CLN-978 用於治療 B 細胞介導的自身免疫疾病。

B 細胞表達 CD19 目標，並在多種自身免疫疾病中發揮作用，這些疾病可能影響多個器官系統。這些疾病的病理解剖共同點是產生針對自身抗原的抗體，這些抗體被稱為自體抗體。學術研究者與產業贊助方已發表資料，涵蓋多種分子目標與治療方式，顯示 CD19xCD3 T 細胞活化劑有潛力在多種難治性自身免疫疾病指標中，包括紅斑狼瘡（SLE）與類風濕性關節炎（RA），實現持續改善疾病表現，包括在某些情況下達成長期症狀緩解。這些臨牀資料顯示，CD19 導向治療導致 B 細胞顯著減少，隨後重新出現 naïve B 細胞組合，對 B 細胞組合產生 "重置" 效果，並持續消除自體反應性抗體。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之分析，並與我們合併財務報表及相關附註說明一併參考。本討論與分析及其他部分包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性，例如有關我們計畫、目標、預期、意圖與預測之陳述。我們實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述所討論者有重大差異。導致此等差異之因素包括，但不僅限於，本年度報告表 10-K 所列之「風險因素」部分所討論者。
我們是一家開發潛在第一或最佳治療方案、高影響力療法之生物製藥公司，用於自身免疫疾病與癌症。我們追求有潛力之治療目標，同時運用在 T 細胞活化劑之核心專業知識，該技術已建立於腫瘤學領域，並正在拓展至自身免疫疾病。我們的臨牀階段產品線建立於嚴謹科學方法與有意圖之創新，我們正推動使命，為患者提供新的照護標準。

• CLN-978 是一種 CD19xCD3 雙特異性 T 細胞活化劑，我們正在開發用於自身免疫疾病。在 Phase 1 OUTRACE 計畫中，CLN-978 正在評估於患有系統性紅斑狼瘡（"SLE"）、類風濕性關節炎（"RA"）及西格蒙德氏症（"SjD"）之患者。OUTRACE SLE 研究為一持續進行之全球 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，針對中度至重度 SLE 患者。OUTRACE RA 研究為一 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，針對活動性、難治性 RA 患者，目前在歐洲進行中。我們預計在 2026 年第二季分享 SLE RA 的初步臨牀數據，並在 2026 年第三季分享 RA 的重複給藥數據。OUTRACE SjD 研究為一持續進行之全球 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，針對活動性、中度至重度西格蒙德氏症患者。我們預計在 2026 年第四季分享西格蒙德氏症的初步臨牀數據。

• Velinotamig 是一種 BCMAxCD3 雙特異性 T 細胞活化劑，我們正在開發用於自身免疫疾病。重慶基因瑞生物製藥有限公司（"Genrix"），我們從該公司取得 velinotamig 的授權，正在中國進行一 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，針對自身免疫疾病患者，最初在 SLE 患者中進行，隨後預計未來擴展至其他適應症，初步臨牀數據預計在 2026 年第四季分享。我們有意利用此 Phase 1 臨牀試驗產生的數據加速全球臨牀發展。完成 Genrix Phase 1 臨牀試驗後，我們將進行所有進一步的 velinotamig 在自身免疫疾病之發展。

• CLN-049 是一種 FLT3xCD3 雙特異性 T 細胞活化劑。CLN-049 正在進行一持續進行之 Phase 1 臨牀試驗，針對曾接受過治療之急性骨髓性白血病（"AML"）或骨髓增生異常綜合症（"MDS"）患者。在 2025 年美國血液學會（"ASH"）年會上，我們分享了來自持續進行之劑量遞增部分的單一療法療效數據，針對曾接受過多重治療之所有來源患者羣體，患有難治性 AML。我們預計在 2026 年第二季分享來自劑量遞增部分的臨牀數據更新。我們也預計在 2026 年第二季開始納入劑量擴展羣組，並預計在 2026 年第四季完成納入，以確定推薦 Phase 2 劑量，用於預期之單臂關鍵性註冊試驗。
• Zipalertinib（CLN-081/TAS6417），我們與太和藥品有限公司（"Taiho"）之子公司合作開發，是一種口服小分子、不可逆表皮生長因子受體（"EGFR"）抑制劑，設計用以選擇性地針對表達 EGFR ex20 插入突變（"EGFR ex20ins"）之細胞，相對地對表達野生型 EGFR 之細胞影響較小。

o 我們正在評估 zipalertinib 在 REZILIENT1 臨牀試驗之關鍵 Phase 2b 部分，針對曾接受過系統治療後進展之 EGFR ex20ins 非小細胞肺癌（"NSCLC"）患者。在 2026 年 2 月，基於 REZILIENT1 之主要療效數據，太和完成了一項新藥申請（"NDA"）的滾動提交，尋求 zipalertinib 用於治療曾接受含鉑系統化學治療之局部晚期或轉移性 EGFR ex20ins NSCLC 患者的加速批准。
o 太和正在評估 zipalertinib 在一全球 Phase 3 臨牀試驗（"REZILIENT3"）中，與化療聯合使用，作為局部晚期或轉移性 EGFR ex20ins NSCLC 成人患者的潛在一線治療。太和在 2026 年 2 月完成試驗納入，預計在 2026 年底取得初步結果。
o Taiho 亦正在評估 zipalertinib 在一項 Phase 2 平行族羣試驗 ("REZILIENT2") 中的應用。Taiho 在 2025 年國際肺癌研究協會 ("IASLC") 世界肺癌會議 ("WCLC") 與歐洲醫學腫瘤學會 ("ESMO") 2025 年大會上，分享了 REZILIENT2 試驗中某些族羣的初步資料。
除了上述產品候選藥物外，我們正積極開發數個預臨牀計畫，用於自身免疫疾病與腫瘤學領域。

CLN-619 是一種 MICA/B 單株抗體，我們先前正在 Phase 1 臨牀試驗中評估。2025 年 5 月，根據對 CLN-619 在子宮內膜癌與子宮頸癌疾病特定擴展族羣的資料評估，我們宣佈停止對患有婦科癌症患者進一步開發 CLN-619，因初步結果未達我們內部的進展門檻。2025 年 11 月，根據對患有非小細胞肺癌與多發性骨髓瘤患者的初步臨牀資料評估，我們停止對 CLN-619 進一步開發。
CLN-617 是一種 interleukin-2 與 interleukin-12 結合蛋白，我們先前正在 Phase 1 臨牀試驗中評估。2025 年 11 月，根據對患有晚期實體腫瘤患者的初步臨牀資料評估，我們停止對 CLN-617 進一步開發。

CLN-418 是一種 B7H4x4-1BB 雙特異性抗體，我們從 Harbour BioMed US Inc. ("Harbour") 取得授權，並先前正在 Phase 1 臨牀試驗中評估。2024 年 8 月，根據對實體腫瘤 Phase 1 臨牀試驗資料的評估，我們通知 Harbour 我們決定終止 CLN-418 的授權與合作協議 ("Harbour License Agreement")，生效日期為 2024 年 11 月。根據終止 Harbour License Agreement，我們停止開發 CLN-418，並將 CLN-418 的開發與商業權利歸還 Harbour。

我們直接持有 CLN-978 的全球智慧財產權。我們持有 velinotamig 的全球智慧財產權，除外中國大陸、香港、澳門及臺灣 (合稱為 "大中華地區")。我們透過一間我們於 2025 年 12 月 31 日擁有 98% 股權的開發子公司，持有 CLN-049 的全球智慧財產權。我們與 Taiho 的附屬公司共同開發 zipalertinib，Taiho 持有該藥物的智慧財產權。我們持有我們早期階段計畫的全球智慧財產權或全球智慧財產權的獨家選擇權。

headings: 與我們產品候選品開發相關的風險
我們可能遭遇重大延遲於臨牀前研究及臨牀試驗，或可能無法按預期時間表進行或完成臨牀前研究或臨牀試驗，甚至可能無法進行或完成。
患者招募困難已導致臨牀試驗延遲，未來也可能導致或阻止我們產品候選品的臨牀試驗，並最終導致或阻止監管審批。
我們目前進行並可能在未來進行產品候選品於美國以外地區的臨牀試驗，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）及相應的外國監管機構可能不會接受來自這些試驗的數據。
我們可能開發與其他療法組合的產品候選品，這將使我們面臨額外的風險。
與我們財務狀況及資金需求相關的風險
我們有限的營運歷史可能使您難以評估我們業務至今的成功情況，並評估我們未來的生存能力。
我們自成立以來已產生重大虧損，且預期在未來幾年內仍將產生虧損，並可能無法實現或維持未來的收入或利潤。
本公司尚未自產品候選品銷售中產生任何收入，且可能永遠無法實現盈利。
若本公司進行收購或策略性合作，可能會增加本公司之資金需求，稀釋股東權益，導致本公司負債或承擔或有負債，並使本公司面臨其他風險。
paragraphs: 下列資訊應與本年度報告表10-K中其他資訊一併閱讀，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，這些資訊出現在本年度報告表10-K的其他地方。發生任何下列所描述的事件或發展，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況或未來結果造成損害，且這些風險因素可能並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或目前認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或未來結果產生不利影響。請參閱本年度報告表10-K中的『特別注意前瞻性陳述』。
我們的前期臨牀研究與臨牀試驗可能無法充分顯示任何產品候選藥物的安全性與有效性，這將會延誤或阻礙開發、監管核准與商業化。

在取得監管核准以進行現有及未來產品候選藥物的商業銷售前，我們必須透過長時間、複雜且昂貴的前期臨牀研究與臨牀試驗，證明我們的 Investigational 產品候選藥物在每一個目標適應症中的安全性與有效性。如果我們進行中或未來的前期臨牀研究與臨牀試驗結果對產品候選藥物的安全性與有效性不夠明確，如果我們未能達到臨牀終點且具有統計學與臨牀意義的顯著性，或如果產品候選藥物存在安全性方面的問題，我們可能會被阻礙或延誤取得該產品候選藥物的市場核准。在某些情況下，由於多種因素，包括臨牀試驗程序的變更與遵循程度、患者羣體的大小與類型差異，以及臨牀試驗參與者退出率的差異，相同產品候選藥物的前期臨牀研究與臨牀試驗在安全性或有效性結果上可能會有顯著差異。

此外，我們與第三方可能對某些適應症的產品候選藥物擁有有限的前期臨牀與臨牀數據，且對這些適應症的整體理解有限，包括自身免疫疾病。我們無法預測產品候選藥物在不同適應症中的安全性與有效性可能有多大差異。我們可能會遇到重大挑戰，以建立適當的模型與試驗方法來評估產品候選藥物的安全性與有效性，也可能無法提供足夠的數據或其他證據，以符合監管機構的要求，使得在前期臨牀與臨牀測試中觀察到的某些意外結果並不代表產品候選藥物的潛在安全性問題。我們可能根據我們在不同適應症中或與其他產品候選藥物的經驗，來制定某些產品候選藥物的計畫與時間表，這些產品候選藥物是基於相同技術開發或整合的。然而，產品候選藥物在不同適應症中開發或與其他產品候選藥物比較時，可能會顯示出意外且重要的差異，包括安全性或有效性方面的差異，這些差異可能需要修改製造程序或臨牀開發計畫，這將需要超出我們最初預期的額外時間與資源。任何這種情況都可能導致我們調整或改變開發計畫，這可能會延誤、損害或阻礙我們開發與商業化或取得這些產品候選藥物的監管核准。

除了我們進行中的 zipalertinib 臨牀試驗外，患者已接受並可能繼續接受 zipalertinib 的擴展使用或『同情使用』計畫治療。如果在該計畫中接受治療的患者經驗與我們進行中或計畫中的公司贊助 zipalertinib 臨牀試驗結果不一致或較不理想，可能會對 zipalertinib、我們的其他產品候選藥物或我們的業務造成負面影響。此外，美國（"美國"）食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）或外國監管機構可能因這些不一致或不理想的結果，要求我們取得並提交額外的臨牀數據，這可能會延誤 zipalertinib 或我們其他產品候選藥物的臨牀開發或市場核准。
前期臨牀與臨牀開發涉及一個長時間且昂貴的過程，結果具有不確定性，且較早期的試驗與試驗結果可能無法預測未來的前期臨牀試驗或臨牀試驗結果。如果我們的前期臨牀試驗與臨牀試驗無法支持任何產品候選藥物的監管核准，我們可能會產生額外成本或遭遇延誤完成，或最終無法完成該產品候選藥物的開發。
